---
title: "Adapting Vib2Sound to missing accelerometer cues"
date: 2026-06-02
description: >
  Vib2Sound separates overlapping zebra finch vocalisations using body-mounted
  accelerometers and multichannel microphones. This project asks how the model can
  stay robust when the accelerometer signal is partly or entirely missing, and which
  strategies best preserve separation performance.
categories: [Speech ML, Neuroscience]
repo: https://github.com/ellacapellini/Vib2Sound
paper: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.08.652866
---

Vib2Sound was introduced by Akahoshi, Wang, Cheng, Zai and Hahnloser (2025). The
**Paper** link above is that original work; the **Code** link is this extension.

**Research question.** How can the separation model be made robust to missing or
degraded accelerometer signals, and what strategies best preserve separation
performance under partial or total cue absence?

Carried out at the Institute of Neuroinformatics (University of Zurich and ETH Zurich),
in the Hahnloser Lab.
